newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Georgia may buy 1.5 mln T Iranian oil in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Georgia may buy 1.5 mln T Iranian oil in 1997.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Georgia may import 1.5 million tonnes of Iranian crude oil this year, Interfax news agency quoted a Georgian energy official as saying on Wednesday.
Gruzneft general director Revaz Tevzadze was quoted as saying that officials from the two countries had met recently in Tehran to discuss economic cooperation, including delivery of energy supplies.
Georgia is also looking to buy one billion cubic metres of natural gas from Iran, Interfax said. The Caucasian republic now imports gas from Russia and Turkmenistan.
There were no details on how Tbilisi would pay for the supplies.
Each year Georgia needs five million tonnes of oil and 3.5 billion cubic metres of natural gas to meet domestic demand.
It produced only 128,000 tonnes of oil and 3.3 million cubic metres of gas last year.
